column2: Your men throw the woman out of your hall.

The people of a far stanitsa speak of a girl who walks out into the snow at night and comes back knowing who will die before the thaw. She has been brought to your hall, barefoot and silent, with eyes the grey of a winter sky. The old women say she has the hag-sight, and that a lord with such a one beside [Root.GetHerHim] will never be taken by surprise. Will you take her in as your wise woman?

A hag of the stanitsa has come to your hall, wrapped in furs and hung with bones and charms against the evil eye. She keeps the old lore of the tribes, speaks with the spirits of the steppe and can smell the taint of Chaos on a man the way a dog smells fear. She asks to stay at your side as your wise woman.

A faint cackle draws your eye to a dark corner of your hall, where a crone is warming her hands at the fire as if she had always been there. No one saw her come in. She tells you she is a hag, that she was old when your grandfather was a boy, and that the spirits have sent her to watch over you. Will you let her stay?

The people of an isolated steading in [Root.Capital.GetName] whisper of a young woman who has the sight. She sees the deaths of men in the smoke of the hearth, and the gods speak to her in the cries of the ravens. She is said to curse or bless whoever she lays eyes on. Will you call her to your hall?

A woman claiming to be a seeress has come to your hall and asks to stay. If the gods truly speak to her, and she can see the fates of men and the coming of storms, she would be worth more to you than a shipful of warriors...

A faint whisper draws your eye to a dark corner of your longhouse, where a haggard crone sits among the dogs. Before you can have her thrown out, she tells you she is a seeress, that the gods have shown her your hall in the smoke, and that she has come to offer you her sight.
She is welcome here.
Send the witch away.

You are sitting with [seeress_mother.GetFirstName], who carries your child, when [seeress_seer.GetFirstName] the hag comes into the chamber unbidden. She points a bony finger at [seeress_mother.GetFirstName]'s belly. "The spirits have spoken to me. The child is tainted! The Ruinous Powers have touched it in the womb, and if it is left to grow it will serve them. When the time comes, the child must be given to the hags."
Guards, remove the witch!
Could it be so? Is the child tainted?

[seeress_seer.GetFirstName] the seeress has been staring at [seeress_mother.GetFirstName] across the hall all evening. At last she gets up, lays her hand on [seeress_mother.GetFirstName]'s belly and closes her eyes. "The ravens circle over this one," she says. "The gods are watching the child you carry. It will be bold, and men will speak of it."
A child of the gods!
The child will grow into the prophecy.

It is the dead of night when a sudden chill wakes you. You sit up and see [From.GetFirstName] standing at the foot of your bed, staring at you without a sound. You rub the sleep from your eyes, and when you look again there is no sign of the child.
Was it a dream?

[From.GetFirstName] is sitting on the floor playing when something dark seems to come over the child. [From.GetSheHeCap] jerks and twists, cries out in a tongue you have never heard, and [From.GetHerHis] eyes roll back until only the whites show.
That cannot be a good sign...

An inhuman wail wakes you, and you rush outside with your axe. On the frozen ground in front of the hall you find [From.GetFirstName], scuttling round and round in circles upside down on all fours, like a spider.
[This.Religion.GetRandomGodNameCap] help me...
[From.GetFirstName] worries you sometimes.

The body of [seeress_victim.GetTitledName] was found today at the bottom of a ravine with a broken neck. It seems a tragic accident, but [seeress_child.GetFirstName] was seen standing at the edge of the ravine, peering down into it, just before the body was found.
Curious...

[seeress_victim.GetTitledName] was found this morning impaled on the fence outside your hall. [seeress_victim.GetSheHeCap] must have fallen from the roof, though what [seeress_victim.GetSheHe] was doing up there no one can say. Little [seeress_child.GetFirstName] was the first to find [seeress_victim.GetHerHim]...
Yes, a strange coincidence...

[seeress_victim.GetTitledName] was found this morning head first in a barrel of rain water, with only [seeress_victim.GetHerHis] pale, stiff legs showing above the rim. The guards say [seeress_victim.GetSheHe] must have tripped and fallen in. [seeress_child.GetFirstName] was playing nearby, but did not see anything.
Yes... I suppose it could have happened that way...

[seeress_seer.GetFirstName] the hag comes to you and demands to see [seeress_child.GetFirstName]. She says the child carries the taint of Chaos, and that it must be burned out in the old way before more evil is done. Give the child to the hags for three nights, she says, and they will do what must be done.
Do as she says. The safety of our people comes first.
Begone! You will not touch my child!
You give your child to the hags.
You refuse the hag.

[seeress_child.GetFirstName] is made to drink a draught the hags have brewed and soon falls into a deep sleep. [seeress_child.GetFirstName]'s mother weeps as [seeress_seer.GetFirstName] wraps the child in a bearskin and carries [seeress_child.GetHerHim] off to the hags' hut at the edge of the woods. For three nights there will be chanting, smoke and fire.
Gods have mercy.
You pace back and forth for three nights.

On the fourth morning [seeress_seer.GetFirstName] carries [seeress_child.GetFirstName] back to your hall, pale and thin and smelling of smoke, but whole. "It is gone," the hag says. "Burned out. Whatever touched the child will not come back." For the first time in years, [seeress_child.GetFirstName] sleeps through the night.
Thank the gods!

On the third night you cannot bear it any longer and break into the hags' hut. [seeress_seer.GetFirstName] is kneeling on [seeress_child.GetFirstName]'s chest with a knife raised over [seeress_child.GetHerHim], chanting. You drag her off before she can strike. The child is cut and burned, but alive, and the hag swears that the taint is gone.
Murderous witch! Banish her!
Let her go. The child was dangerous.

On the fourth morning [seeress_seer.GetFirstName] comes to your hall alone, her hands still stained red. "It had to be done," she says. "The taint was too deep. It would not come out of the child, so I sent the child to the spirits with it." [seeress_child.GetFirstName]'s small body lies wrapped in the bearskin in the hags' hut.
You murderous witch! Execute her!
Banish her!
She did what was needed.

On the third night screams from the hags' hut wake the whole stanitsa. When you get there with torches, what is left of [seeress_seer.GetFirstName] is spread across the floor and the walls, and [seeress_child.GetFirstName] is sitting in the blood, playing. The child gives you a curious look, gets up and walks home to bed as if nothing had happened. No hag will come near [seeress_child.GetHerHim] again.
What has happened here?

All your life the voices have whispered to you in the dark: in your cradle, at play, at the edge of the ravine. Tonight, as you come of age, they speak plainly at last, and give you their names. You know now who has been watching over you, and whom you belong to.
I hear you, my masters.

Before you were born, a seeress laid her hand on your mother's belly and said the gods were watching you. You have heard the tale all your life, and now that you are grown, the men of your father's hall look at you as if they expect great things. You mean to give them what they expect.
The gods chose well.
